# CLI reference

The `openbrick` command line builds, validates and calibrates brick-compatible parts. This page is the `--help` text of every command, taken from the program built from this repository, so it matches that version; `openbrick <command> --help` prints the same text. [Install](guides/install.md) describes how to get the command, and the [first print test](guides/print-test.md) walks through it from the calibration coupon to a printed tile.

## `openbrick`

```text
OpenBrick3D: brick-compatible part designer, assembler and print pipeline

Usage: openbrick <COMMAND>

Commands:
  standard   Print the Dimensional Standard v1 (nominal mm, LDU, confidence)
  profiles   List bundled process profiles
  check      Structurally check a part document (.obpart.json)
  about      Print the non-affiliation disclaimer and attribution
  build      Build a part into a printable 3MF or STL (validated first)
  calibrate  Print the calibration coupon and record the cells that fit best
  validate   Validate a part against a process and fit profile
  convert    Convert between .obrick, .ldr/.mpd, 3MF, STL, glTF (M3)
  run        Run a batch merch job (M4)
  serve      Serve the PWA on the LAN with a QR code (M4)
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Exit codes: 0 success; 1 the validator found blockers (nothing written); 2 usage or input error; 3 internal error or not implemented yet.
```

## `openbrick build`

```text
Build a part into a printable 3MF or STL (validated first).

The part is validated first: with blockers nothing is written and the exit code is 1.

Usage: openbrick build [OPTIONS] --out <FILE> <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          Part document (.obpart.json). Asset paths inside it (such as the default logo assets/mark.svg) are relative to the part file's folder

Options:
  -p, --param <NAME=VALUE>
          Set a parameter, NAME=VALUE; repeat for more. Footprints as 2x4 (or [2,4]), lengths in mm (0.6 or 0.6mm), enum options by value (relief=inlay), booleans as true/false. SVG and other asset parameters are file paths relative to the current directory (logo=./my-logo.svg)

      --params <NAME=VALUE>...
          Several parameters at once (--params size=2x4 relief=inlay); put the part file before it

      --process <ID>
          Process profile id (see `openbrick profiles`). Default: the fit profile's process when --fit is given and the part allows it, else the first entry of the part's print.profiles

      --fit <PATH|example>
          Fit profile: a fit profile JSON written by `openbrick calibrate record`, or `example` for the bundled example (a starting point, not a calibration of your printer; use ./example for a file of that name). Fit-critical parts (studs, tubes) are blocked without one (FIT.MISSING)

      --json
          Print one JSON object on stdout (report per schemas/report.schema.json, measurements, content hash, outputs, timings); human text goes to stderr

  -o, --out <FILE>
          Output file. .3mf: one object whose parts are the colour roles (body, accent), each part with its own filament in the slicer, plus traceability metadata. .stl: one single-colour solid. Missing folders are created

      --fuse
          3MF only: write one fused single-colour object instead of one part per colour role

      --no-colour
          3MF only: leave out the display colours. The parts stay as they are, and you give each part its filament in the slicer as usual. For Bambu Studio 2.5 and later, whose "Standard 3MF Import color" dialog is reported to paint a 3MF's colours onto the surface instead of giving each part a filament (bambulab/BambuStudio#9666); without colours it has nothing to read (docs/spikes/q18-slicer-multimaterial-import.md)

          [alias: --no-color]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  openbrick build parts/ndn.logo-tile.obpart.json --fit example --out tile.3mf
  openbrick build parts/ndn.logo-tile.obpart.json --param logo=./my-logo.svg --param relief=inlay --fit my-fit.json --out inlay.3mf
  openbrick build parts/ndn.logo-tile.obpart.json --params relief=inlay inlayStyle=parts --fit my-fit.json --out inlay-parts.3mf
  openbrick build parts/ndn.logo-tile.obpart.json --params size=2x2 height=brick --fit my-fit.json --out tile.stl --json

Exit codes: 0 written; 1 blockers (nothing written; each blocker is printed with its rule, measured value, threshold and fix); 2 usage or input error; 3 internal error.
```

## `openbrick calibrate`

```text
Print the calibration coupon and record the cells that fit best

Usage: openbrick calibrate <COMMAND>

Commands:
  coupon  Build the calibration coupon as 3MF or STL
  record  Record the coupon cells that fit best as a fit profile
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

Examples:
  openbrick calibrate coupon --process fdm-0.4 --out coupon.3mf --manifest coupon.json
  openbrick calibrate coupon --pockets full --bed 256x256 --out coupon-full.3mf
  openbrick calibrate record --process fdm-0.4 --printer "Prusa MINI+" --material PLA --stud 4.80 --tube 4.95 --pocket 6.65/0.30 --out my-fit.json

Guide: docs/guides/print-test.md
```

## `openbrick calibrate coupon`

```text
Build the calibration coupon as 3MF or STL.

Prints which cell is which. Print it flat side down with no supports, press genuine bricks onto the cells and record the best fit with `calibrate record`.

Usage: openbrick calibrate coupon [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --process <ID>
          Process profile id the coupon is printed with (see `openbrick profiles`)

          [default: fdm-0.4]

      --pockets <SET>
          Which 2x2 pockets (tube OD x rib depth) to print: cross (the default, fits a 180 x 180 mm bed), cross-and-diagonal or full (larger beds). Record with the same --pocket-set

          [default: cross]

      --bed <XxY>
          Bed size the coupon must fit, XxY in mm (default 180x180, a Prusa MINI+ or Bambu Lab A1 mini; 5 mm stay free at each edge)

      --copies <N>
          Identical copies of the cell set, for repeatability (default 2)

  -o, --out <FILE>
          Output file, .3mf or .stl (default coupon-<process>-<pockets>.3mf)

      --manifest <FILE>
          Also write the cell map as JSON: what --json prints, with the output path relative to the manifest

      --json
          Print one JSON object on stdout; human text goes to stderr

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `openbrick calibrate record`

```text
Record the coupon cells that fit best as a fit profile.

The offsets are the chosen cell minus the standard nominal; pass the file to `build --fit`.

Usage: openbrick calibrate record [OPTIONS] --process <ID> --printer <PRINTER> --material <MATERIAL> --out <FILE>

Options:
      --process <ID>
          Process profile id the coupon was printed with

      --printer <PRINTER>
          Printer name, for example "Prusa MINI+"

      --material <MATERIAL>
          Material type, for example PLA or PETG

      --brand <BRAND>
          Material brand (optional)

      --nozzle <MM>
          Nozzle diameter in mm

          [default: 0.4]

      --slicer <SLICER>
          Slicer and version, for example "PrusaSlicer 2.9.2"

          [default: ""]

      --intent <INTENT>
          What the fit aims at: fits-genuine-bricks or fits-itself

          [default: fits-genuine-bricks]

      --id <ID>
          Profile id (default: derived from printer, material and process)

      --author <AUTHOR>
          Who calibrated (default anonymous)

      --date <YYYY-MM-DD>
          Calibration date, YYYY-MM-DD (default: today, UTC)

      --notes <NOTES>
          Free-text notes

      --pocket-set <SET>
          The pocket set of the coupon you printed: cross (default), cross-and-diagonal or full

          [default: cross]

      --stud <MM>
          Best stud cell (outer diameter, mm), as its label shows it

      --tube <MM>
          Best tube bore cell (inner diameter, mm)

      --pocket <OD/RIB>
          Best 2x2 pocket as its two-line label reads, tube OD over rib depth, for example 6.65/0.30. A pocket is one choice: both numbers come from the same cell

      --pocket-tube-od <MM>
          The best pocket's tube OD (with --pocket-rib; same as --pocket OD/RIB)

      --pocket-rib <MM>
          The best pocket's rib depth (with --pocket-tube-od)

      --technic-h <MM>
          Best horizontal Technic hole cell (inner diameter, mm)

      --pin <MM>
          Best Technic pin cell (outer diameter, mm)

      --axle <MM>
          Best axle-hole cell (cross envelope, mm)

      --bar <MM>
          Best bar cell (diameter, mm)

      --clip <MM>
          Best clip cell (opening, mm)

  -o, --out <FILE>
          Where to write the fit profile (JSON)

      --json
          Print one JSON object on stdout; human text goes to stderr

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `openbrick validate`

```text
Validate a part against a process and fit profile.

Prints the validator report; the exit code is 1 when it has blockers.

Usage: openbrick validate [OPTIONS] <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          Part document (.obpart.json). Asset paths inside it (such as the default logo assets/mark.svg) are relative to the part file's folder

Options:
  -p, --param <NAME=VALUE>
          Set a parameter, NAME=VALUE; repeat for more. Footprints as 2x4 (or [2,4]), lengths in mm (0.6 or 0.6mm), enum options by value (relief=inlay), booleans as true/false. SVG and other asset parameters are file paths relative to the current directory (logo=./my-logo.svg)

      --params <NAME=VALUE>...
          Several parameters at once (--params size=2x4 relief=inlay); put the part file before it

      --process <ID>
          Process profile id (see `openbrick profiles`). Default: the fit profile's process when --fit is given and the part allows it, else the first entry of the part's print.profiles

      --fit <PATH|example>
          Fit profile: a fit profile JSON written by `openbrick calibrate record`, or `example` for the bundled example (a starting point, not a calibration of your printer; use ./example for a file of that name). Fit-critical parts (studs, tubes) are blocked without one (FIT.MISSING)

      --json
          Print one JSON object on stdout (report per schemas/report.schema.json, measurements, content hash, outputs, timings); human text goes to stderr

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
